newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador vows to press ahead with telcomms sale.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador vows to press ahead with telcomms sale.

text.p: El Salvador President Armando Calderon Sol pledged on Monday to work with opposition legislators to pass a law allowing the state-owned telephone company to be privatized.
"There is no point beyond discussion, we can discuss the issue and find a solution," Calderon Sol told reporters.
Salvadorean lawmakers last week vetoed a government bill to allow the sale of the Administracion Nacional de Telecommunicaciones (ANTEL).
By law, Calderon Sol can overrule the veto and uphold the bill, but he said he wanted to address the opposition's objections in order to win consensus on the sale.
Legislators from the leftist Farabundo Marti National Liberation Front fear the company will be sold to foreigners and want the government to keep control.
"One percent more, one percent less, whether or not voting control is in the hands of foreigners...these are surmountable problems," Calderon Sol said.

The government wants to sell ANTEL to modernize the company. The winning buyer is expected to invest some $3 billion in the company in the next 10 years. The company has been priced at between $300 million and $1 billion.
